text:
Edmonton's 3-1 win in San Jose was decided in 2 minutes and 27 seconds of the third period. Vasily Podkolzin broke a one-goal game open at 3:13, and Alex Formenton added a backhand at 5:40, both at even strength, to make it 3-0. Before that, the Oilers had led only on a Mattias Ekholm slap shot from the first period that had a 3 percent chance of going in, and the game was tight and quiet through the middle.

The underlying numbers say the margin was earned. EDM generated 3.07 expected goals to SJS's 1.28 and held a 50-43 edge in shot attempts, and a simulated replay of every shot gives the Oilers the win 77 percent of the time. The third period was where it tilted: EDM out-chanced SJS 2.38 to 0.66 in expected goals, after SJS had edged the second 0.46 to 0.20. Connor McDavid skated 24:06, had an assist on Podkolzin's goal, and was on the ice for 2.22 expected goals for and 0.23 against. He also had a 31 percent look in the third that Yaroslav Askarov stopped. Tristan Jarry stopped 19 of 20 shots, a shade better than the 1.28 goals expected against him.

Macklin Celebrini made it 3-1 at 11:19 on a wrist shot, assisted by Michael Misa, and that was as close as SJS came. Neither team scored on the power play (EDM 0 for 2, SJS 0 for 1). Askarov allowed 3 goals on 2.66 expected, so he was roughly in line with the chances he faced. Both teams put 20 shots on goal, but EDM's were the better ones.
